Datadog generated elite cash conversion in Q3 2026 with Operating Cash Flow of $289.95M and Reported Free Cash Flow of $279.08M (23.3% FCF margin). Deducting non-cash stock compensation of $9.51M yields True Economic Free Cash Flow of $269.57M.

• Negative Working Capital Dynamic: Multi-year enterprise upfront billings continue to create positive working capital float.
Row 4: Operational Wins, Drags & Earnings Call Q&A Audit
QUALITATIVE & TRANSCRIPT FORENSICS

Operational Wins & Catalysts

  • Accelerating Hyper-Growth: Q3 revenue grew 35.2% YoY to $1,197.09M, exceeding expectations by +$50.12M (+4.37%).
  • Enterprise Account Expansion: Large enterprise customers ($100K+ ARR) climbed to 4,860, up 20% YoY with 240 net additions.
  • GAAP Gross Margin Expansion: Gross margin rose to 80.19%, benefiting from proprietary multi-cloud data pipeline efficiency.
  • AI Observability Momentum: AI-native customers now account for over 6% of ARR, while traditional enterprise LLM tracing is surging.

Execution Drags & Watch Items

  • GAAP EPS Noise: GAAP diluted EPS of $0.32 was below $0.64 consensus due to tax provisions and specialized AI R&D staffing.
  • Cloud Optimization Scrutiny: While enterprise spending has stabilized, customers continue to scrutinize log retention tiers.
  • Sales & Marketing Expansion: S&M expenses rose to $303.30M as Datadog aggressively builds out enterprise field engineering.
  • Multi-Product Adoption Ceiling: Customers using 4+ products reached 49%, requiring continued product velocity to cross 60%.

Top Institutional Analyst Q&A and Analyst Questions Forensic Exchanges

Sanjit Singh (Morgan Stanley) AI Workload Monitoring Monetization & Customer Usage Trajectory

Question: Olivier, you noted that 35% YoY revenue growth was fueled in part by digital operations and AI workloads. Can you quantify the direct contribution from AI-native customers and how traditional enterprises are using Datadog to monitor their LLMs?

Executive Answer: Olivier Pomel (CEO) replied: 'AI is rapidly becoming a pervasive driver across our platform. AI-native customers represent over 6% of our ARR and are growing at triple-digit rates. But more importantly, traditional enterprises are now deploying LLM models into production, and they require Datadog for tracing, latency debugging, and token cost governance. We see AI accelerating cloud data consumption across all three pillars.'

Brad Zelnick (Deutsche Bank) Gross Margin Sustainability & Infrastructure Efficiency

Question: David, GAAP gross margin expanded to 80.19% and Non-GAAP was above 82%. What drove the efficiency in cloud hosting costs, and is this 80%+ level sustainable into 2027?

Executive Answer: David Obstler (CFO) responded: 'Our gross margin performance reflects ongoing structural engineering optimizations across our data processing pipeline. We've optimized our multi-cloud architecture and tiering of log data. While we continue to reinvest in new AI capabilities, we feel very comfortable with gross margins remaining in the low-to-mid 80s range.'

Kash Rangan (Goldman Sachs) Platform Consolidation & Multi-Product Cross-Selling Momentum

Question: Olivier, with 4,860 customers now over $100K ARR, how much of the growth is coming from customers consolidating disjointed point solutions into the Datadog platform?

Executive Answer: Olivier Pomel explained: 'Consolidation is our primary growth engine. CIOs are actively eliminating separate vendors for APM, infrastructure, logs, and cloud security. Over 49% of our customers now use four or more products, and our security products continue to show the fastest adoption curves in our history. The Datadog unified data model is an unbeatable value proposition.'
